name: How_To_Clean_Jewelery->Article
text: Over time, jewelry can become dull or tarnished. Rather than allowing your jewels to simply sit in your jewelry box, never to be worn, there are many ways to polish your collections on your own. Discover how to take care of your jewelry with these DIY at home tips! Keep your jewelry as beautiful and glimmering as the day you purchased it. Silver Care The following at home methods which work well for both solid and sterling silver jewelry pieces: • Baking Soda- Baking soda works great to remove tarnish from silver. Mix three parts baking soda to one-part water. Wet the silver and apply the paste with a soft cloth, work into the piece of jewelry and rinse well and buff dry. • Toothpaste- Apply a dab of white toothpaste to tarnished silver and rub gently with a soft cloth. Rinse well with warm water and buff dry! • Window Cleaner- Spray window cleaner on a toothbrush and use it to gently scrub your sterling silver and watch it return to its shiny state. • Laundry Detergent- Line a bowl with aluminum foil and fill it with hot water. Mix in one tablespoon of powdered laundry detergent, then soak your silver for one minute. Rinse with clean water and air dry. Gold Care Even though gold does not tarnish as easily as silver, it may lose its shine every now and then. The following are home methods for solid gold jewelry items only (not gold-plated): • Dish Detergent- Mix some dish detergent in warm water. Gently brush the gold with a toothbrush and place in warm water to rinse. Air dry! - to restore the shine of gemstones, the above instructions may be used but instead of using regular water, mix the dish detergent with seltzer water. • Vinegar- Pour white vinegar into a bowl and let your gold jewelry sit in it for twenty minutes. Rinse carefully with lukewarm water and dry with a soft cloth. • Beer- Pour beer into a soft cloth. Rub it up and down over your gold piece evenly. Rinse in water and pat dry. • Ammonia- Pour half a tablespoon of ammonia in a bowl, add half a glass of water, and mix together. Soak your jewelry in the mixture for no more than a minute, then remove with tongs. Rinse under running water and dry with a soft cloth. Please note that cleaning jewelry with ammonia should not be done for delicate gemstones and pearls. Gold plated jewelry: • Soap Water: Pour soap water into a bowl and dip an old toothbrush in it. Scratch off the dirt on your gold-plated jewelry gently. Rose gold jewelry: • Line a bowl with aluminum foil (shiny side up), fill with warm water, add 1 tablespoon salt, 1 tablespoon baking soda, and half a tablespoon dishwashing liquid. Stir evenly and allow the rose-gold jewelry to sit in it for 10-15 minutes. Rinse with water and dry with soft cloth. Ring Care How to clean rings when in a hurry? Keep a jewelry cleaning stick with you. Twist the wand to release the cleaner and use the soft brush tip to remove any dirt. Rinse well! From Morning to Night Jewelry should be the last thing you put on after your morning routine. Apply makeup and perfumes first so they do not contaminate your jewels, as well as put on clothes first so they do not catch on your jewelry. Once headed out of the house, avoid the sun- just as the sun's rays can harm our skin, they can also damage our jewels! It is also recommended not to wear jewelry while swimming- chlorine and salt can damage it! At the end of the day, store your jewelry in a jewelry box, each piece separated from one another, therefore nothing gets scratched or tangled. In addition, do not sleep in your jewelry- sleeping can harm the jewelry, as well-it is safer for you!
